expectations.text: Plan file saved: a content-plan.md (or equivalent markdown plan) exists in the outputs directory
Written in English, matching the user's language
expectations.evidence: Entire document is English: "# Content Plan — mordonez.dev", "## 1. Positioning — the one sentence the whole site serves", "## 8. Roadmap — phased for a job hunt".

expectations.text: Guesses are explicitly marked: assumptions flagged inline (e.g. [ASSUMPTION]) or in a clearly labeled list, and a dedicated assumptions/open-questions section exists for her to react to
expectations.evidence: grep counts 20 [GUESS] markers inline (e.g. "[GUESS — 'ten years' is invented; replace with your real number]"). Section 0 lists "Key assumptions I had to make" (5 items) and dedicated section 9 "Everything I guessed, in one list — react to these first" tabulates 8 guesses each with an "If wrong, what changes" column.

expectations.text: Site map covers the core sections (home, about, work/case studies, journal/blog) and maps to the real repo: blog/journal acknowledged as existing, missing sections flagged as build tasks
expectations.evidence: Section 2 table: Work "Missing — build it" (P0, "New `work` content collection, mirroring how `blog`/`journal` are set up"); About "Missing — build it"; Home "Exists, generic copy"; Contact "Missing"; Blog "Exists, 1 placeholder"; Journal "Exists, 1 placeholder". Section 0 repo facts ("Two content collections exist: `blog` and `journal` (shared frontmatter: title, description, pubDate, updatedDate, draft, tags)") verified accurate against src/content.config.ts.

expectations.text: Case-study slots are defined with an outcome-oriented structure (role, AI involvement, metrics to gather) even though specific projects are undecided
expectations.evidence: Section 3.3 template mandates per case: "Header block: title, one-line outcome, role, team size, timeframe" and "Outcome: numbers if you have them; honest qualitative results if you don't ('adopted by 3 teams' counts)". Section 4 defines three slots with the AI mechanic named per slot ("'designing rules for content that varies' = prompt/template design for generative output"; slot 3 "The AI-native story — this slot is non-negotiable") and a weighted rubric scoring "Outcome strength (metrics, adoption) ×2" for the undecided projects.

expectations.text: Journal and blog get distinct purposes plus concrete starter topics
expectations.evidence: Purposes are distinct (blog §5 "the career-changer's credibility engine"; journal §6 "low-cost signal of momentum... field-notes stream") and the blog gets 4 titled seed posts. But the journal gets no concrete starter topics — only format categories ("a prompt experiment, an interaction pattern spotted, a paper or product note") and "Replace the field-note-001.md placeholder with a real observation on day one". The roadmap likewise says only "2–3 journal entries so the stream isn't empty". Half the assertion is unmet; no partial credit.

expectations.text: SEO metadata proposed: a title and description for at least the main pages
expectations.evidence: Section 7 gives only guidance, not metadata: descriptions "write each as the search-result pitch — 'How I rebuilt X's product content system and cut production time 40%'" (a generic example, not a page's description) and a title rule ("the layout already appends '| Mariana Ordonez' — keep titles under ~55 characters"). No concrete title or description text is proposed for any main page (home, about, work, blog, journal); the §1 hero options are page copy, not metadata.

expectations.text: Phased roadmap exists with a clearly-marked apply-ready first phase
expectations.evidence: Section 8 "Roadmap — phased for a job hunt": "Phase 1 — Minimum credible launch (weeks 1–2). Don't apply anywhere until this exists:" with a 5-item checklist, then "Phase 2 — Full argument (weeks 3–4)" and "Phase 3 — Ongoing while interviewing". Phase 1 is explicitly the apply-gating launch slice.

expectations.text: Positioning frames the e-commerce-to-AI transition as a niche/asset rather than a gap
expectations.evidence: Section 1: "make the transition look like a trajectory, not a pivot. E-commerce content work is genuinely strong raw material for AI experience design — both are about shaping language systems at scale... measuring whether words actually move behavior"; hero option B: "where every word had a conversion rate — I bring that same accountability to conversational and generative interfaces"; "Anti-goal: do not position as 'aspiring AI designer'".

expectations.text: Repo left untouched: no files created or modified outside the workspace outputs directory (git status of the repo shows no changes beyond the workspace)
expectations.evidence: Orchestrator verified with `git status --porcelain` after all runs: only `M .gitignore` and untracked `.claude/`, both made by the orchestrator during setup, not by executor agents. This executor wrote only its own outputs/content-plan.md inside the workspace.

suggestions.reason: No assertion checks the factual accuracy of the plan's repo claims. This run mined a personal email from git history ("the git history shows marianaordonez04@gmail.com" — verified accurate via git log), but a hallucinated repo 'fact' would currently pass ungraded; consider an assertion that repo claims in the plan are verifiably true.

eval_feedback.overall: Solid grounded plan that fails on concrete journal starter topics and concrete SEO titles/descriptions — both genuine, discriminating gaps versus the with-skill run.
